content.text: Section 9.4 matches the preferred position verbatim in substance, and my sweep confirms no Vendor convenience right or early-termination fee exists anywhere in the document.

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.
input.rationale:
Section 9.4 meets the preferred position on every material term: (i) Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on thirty days' prior written notice; (ii) Vendor must promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period, with Customer owing Fees only for conforming Services rendered through the termination date; and (iii) Vendor is expressly denied any corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term. No early-termination fee or penalty is imposed. A full sweep of the termination provisions (§§ 9.1-9.5, 10.1-10.2) and the balance of the document found no Vendor convenience right anywhere — the Vendor's only exit routes are mutual ones for material breach (§ 9.1) and insolvency (§ 9.2), and § 24.4 further bars Vendor from terminating on Customer's change of control. This is favourable to us and is not redlined.

One tension to note without flagging here: § 2.1 commits Customer to USD 2,000,000 per year for three years on a take-or-pay basis "without reduction or termination rights," which economically undercuts the § 9.4 convenience right even though it does not remove it. That is a minimum-commitment problem rather than a termination-clause defect, and per the playbook's no-double-flagging principle it belongs under the MINCOMMIT rule, not T4C. The termination architecture itself sits at the preferred position.
